# Egap.Documents.Markdown: guide for coding agents

Egap.Documents.Markdown is the Markdown add-on for Egap.Documents: CommonMark 0.31 with GitHub's extensions and YAML front
matter read into the document model, and the model written as GitHub Flavored Markdown, with images, footnotes, task
lists and tables; and Markdown to PDF. Parsing is Markdig's.

Namespaces: `Egap.Documents` (`MarkdownFormat` and its options keep the names they had in Egap.Documents 1.x), and
`Egap.Documents.Pdf` for `PdfConvert.FromMarkdown` and `SaveAsPdf`.

## Egap's vocabulary

Egap has its own names. Use them, not names from other PDF, Word or Excel libraries: there is no `PdfReader`, `PdfWriter`,
`XWPFDocument`, `Range.Text` or `IWorkbook` in Egap.

- `PdfDocument` (namespace `Egap.Pdf`) is a PDF file: `PdfDocument.Open`, `PdfDocument.Create`, `PdfDocument.Merge`, then
  `Pages`, `Metadata`, `Outline`, `Form`, `Attachments`, `Signatures` and `Save`. It is `IDisposable` and keeps its file open
  until disposed.
- `Document` (namespace `Egap.Documents`) is a flow document: one model for DOCX, DOC, RTF, ODT, plain text, PDF, HTML,
  MHTML, EPUB and Markdown. `Document.Load` and `Save` pick the format; `DocumentBuilder` edits at a cursor. It is not
  disposable.
- `Workbook` and `Worksheet` (namespace `Egap.Spreadsheets`) are an Excel workbook and its sheets; `sheet["B2"]` is a
  `Cell`, `sheet.Range("A1:C9")` a `CellRange`, and `CellValue` a cell's value.
- Each format has its own class (`DocxFormat`, `RtfFormat`, `OdtFormat`, `TextFormat`, `HtmlFormat`, `EpubFormat`,
  `MarkdownFormat`) and members on `Document` that forward to it: `Document.LoadDocx`, `SaveAsDocx`, `ToHtml`,
  `SaveAsMarkdown`. `SaveAsPdf` and `PdfConvert` (namespace `Egap.Documents.Pdf`) write PDF.
- Options are objects with `init` properties, set in an object initializer and passed to the call: `PdfReadOptions`,
  `PdfSaveOptions`, `PdfRenderOptions`, `PdfExportOptions`, `PdfConvertOptions`, `LayoutOptions`, `WorkbookLoadOptions`.
- Damaged input is repaired and reported, not thrown: `pdf.Warnings` (`PdfWarning`), a `Load` overload with
  `out IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning>`, and the list `Document.Save` returns. A `Strict` option throws instead.
- Sizes are PDF points (1/72 inch). `Length.Mm(15)`, `Length.Cm`, `Length.In` and `Length.Pt` (namespace `Egap.Pdf`) turn
  into points by themselves. Page indexes in code count from 0; `PdfPageRange.Parse("1-3,z")` takes page numbers from 1.
- Images, fonts and drawing come from Egami: a page renders to an Egami `Raster<Rgba8>` (namespaces `Egami` and
  `Egami.Pixels`), and draws onto any Egami.Drawing `Canvas`.
- Egap never opens a network connection by itself: the resolver, base folder or `HttpClient` you pass decides what a
  document may fetch.

## Entry points

- `MarkdownFormat.Register()` once at startup: `Document.Load`, `Document.Save` and `PdfConvert.FromFile` then handle
  `.md` and `.markdown`. Calling `MarkdownFormat` or the `Document` members directly needs no registration.
- `Document.LoadMarkdown(path)`, `Document.ParseMarkdown(text)` and `MarkdownFormat.Load(path, MarkdownLoadOptions)`:
  Markdown to a document. `Extensions` (`MarkdownExtensions.GitHub` by default, `None` for plain CommonMark) and
  `ImageResolver` are the options.
- `doc.ToMarkdown()`, `doc.SaveAsMarkdown(path, MarkdownSaveOptions)` and `MarkdownFormat.Save`: a document as Markdown.
  `Images` (`MarkdownImageMode.Files`, `DataUris`, `Placeholders`, `Omit`), `ImagesFolder`, `ImageResolver`,
  `ImageWriter`, `WriteFrontMatter`, `FigureResolution`, `VectorFiguresAsSvg` and `RevisionView` are the options.
- `PdfConvert.FromMarkdown(markdown, outputPath, PdfConvertOptions)`: Markdown text to PDF in one call; with a
  `TableOfContents` it fills a `[TOC]` paragraph.

## Samples

Markdown in and out, and Markdown to PDF:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;
using Egap.Documents.Pdf;

MarkdownFormat.Register();                                       // once at startup: Document.Load and Save know .md
Document notes = Document.LoadMarkdown("notes.md");
notes.SaveAsDocx("notes.docx");
string markdown = Document.LoadDocx("report.docx").ToMarkdown();
PdfConvert.FromMarkdown("# Hello", "hello.pdf");
```

Choose the extensions read:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;

Document readme = MarkdownFormat.Load("README.md", new MarkdownLoadOptions { Extensions = MarkdownExtensions.GitHub });
```

Write a DOCX as Markdown with front matter and SVG figures:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;

Document report = Document.Load("report.docx");
report.SaveAsMarkdown("report.md", new MarkdownSaveOptions { WriteFrontMatter = true, VectorFiguresAsSvg = true });
```

## Common mistakes

- `Document.Load("notes.md")` before `MarkdownFormat.Register()`: it throws a `NotSupportedException` that names this
  package. A `.txt` file loads as plain text, not Markdown.
- Expecting images to be fetched. Nothing is read unless `MarkdownLoadOptions.ImageResolver` returns the bytes; an image
  left unfetched becomes a picture that links to its URL. `PdfConvert.FromFile` reads a file's images from its own
  folder, never from the network.
- Losing pictures on save. Pictures without an address go to a folder beside the file (`<name>.images`) by default; with a
  stream or `ToMarkdown` give an `ImageResolver`, or choose `DataUris` (which GitHub does not show) or `Omit`.
- Ignoring the warnings. Markdown holds less than the model, and each thing left out comes back from
  `SaveAsMarkdown` as a `ConversionWarning`.
- Expecting CRLF or another encoding: Markdown is written as UTF-8 with LF line ends.
